skill.displayName: 一站式学术Journal Club PPT制作技能，从PDF直达组会演示PPT！

llm.summary: This skill gives guidance for creating and checking academic slide decks from research PDFs, with no hidden or disproportionate behavior found.

dimensions.detail: Creating project folders, rendering PDFs, cropping figures, and using local document-processing tools are proportionate to the slide-generation workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is markdown-only with no executable installer, but one reference mentions local virtualenv installs of common Python packages without pinned versions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to user-directed deck creation and quality checks; I found no prompt hijacking, unrelated authority requests, hidden data flows, or instructions to override agent safeguards.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill may create normal project outputs and an optional local virtual environment, but it does not request elevated privileges, background services, scheduled tasks, credential access, or cross-session persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to build figure-first journal club slides from research papers, and the instructions focus on paper analysis, figure extraction, slide design, and render QA consistent with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install appears reasonable for a slide-generation skill. If dependencies are needed, use a local virtual environment and prefer pinned, reviewed package versions from a trusted package index, especially when processing private papers or unpublished research.
llm.findings: [T08] expected: The reference to installing pymupdf, python-pptx, pillow, and markitdown supports the scanner's supply-chain caution because versions are not pinned, but the packages are purpose-aligned document/slide tooling and no malicious dependency source or executable payload is present.
